reasons: All atomic fallback elements are present in operative text: Licensor retains generic tools and know-how, and Licensee takes a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the deliverables for its business.

The disapplication of Article II(g) (modification consent), Article VI (sublicensing consent) and Article XXI(a) (licence termination) is necessary, not surplus: without it the granted rights to modify, sublicense and hold a perpetual/irrevocable licence would be defeated by the untouched clauses.
Preferred level is unmet (no assignment of deliverables, no embedded-IP licence, no Customer Data retention, no anti-joint-ownership statement), which is acceptable given the locked fallback target.

Single insertion; all other commercial terms, the post-termination return and certification mechanics, and the Licensor ownership of the Licensed Technology remain effective, so no contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced. Only note: confirm the cross-reference "Article VII(b)" matches the numbering of the further-development paragraph as executed.
